newsitem.title: UK: Commerce's Daley sees progress between EU and Boeing.
newsitem.headline: Commerce's Daley sees progress between EU and Boeing.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said Wednesday that he was hopeful that progress could be made between the European Commission and U.S. aircraft giant Boeing Co. over its proposed $14 billion takeover of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The European Union has threatened to block the deal on antitrust grounds.
"We are optimistic that progress will be made between the parties," Daley told reporters.
"We obviously believe this merger is good for the companies, good for competitiveness and good for customers around the world."
He said he did not think the Commission was saying the deal could not take place. "What they are saying is that there are ramifications if it goes ahead and they will act on those."
But he declined to say say whether the Clinton administration thought a Commission move to block the merger would have any legal force.

The EU will announce its final decision on July 23. EU officials said last week that the plan in its current state was "not sufficient" under EU antitrust laws and threatened to block it if changes were not made.
